data.content_ref: inline:{"analogy":null,"claim":"The night-time UHI is primarily a boundary-layer depth effect: calm, clear nights form a shallow, stable rural boundary layer in which radiative cooling concentrates, while the urban canopy layer remains mechanically mixed by the urban canopy's roughness and residual warmth, distributing stored heat through a deeper layer; the cross-city gap scales with building height and built density because taller, rougher canopies sustain deeper mixing and slower cooling.","counterconditions":[{"case":"If the nocturnal UHI is strongest under completely windless conditions with no measurable turbulence, the mixing-depth mechanism is disfavored.","checker_spec":null,"eval":"observation"},{"case":"If rural and urban boundary layers are measured to be the same depth but the UHI persists, the boundary-layer-depth explanation fails.","checker_spec":null,"eval":"observation"},{"case":"If reducing building height while keeping thermal mass and SVF constant eliminates the UHI, the roughness-mixing mechanism is confirmed; if not, it is not primary.","checker_spec":null,"eval":"observation"}],"definitions":[],"derivation":[],"formalization_refs":[],"mechanism":"Under clear, calm conditions, rural surfaces cool radiatively, forming a shallow, stable inversion layer near the ground; the cooling is concentrated in a thin layer, producing low air temperatures. In the city, the roughness sublayer generated by building height and street canyon geometry maintains turbulent mixing even under nominally calm synoptic conditions, preventing the formation of a shallow inversion and mixing stored sensible heat from the urban canopy through a deeper layer. The surface can still cool, but the near-surface air temperature remains higher because the heat is distributed vertically rather than concentrated. Cross-city, taller buildings and denser street canopies increase roughness and mixing depth, making the nocturnal UHI more pronounced.","premises":[],"schema":"deepreason-reasoning-envelope-v1","scope":{"covers":[],"excludes":[]},"simulation_refs":[],"uncertainties":[]}
